body:
PROCEDURE: waits and handoffs (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-05 18:55Z, draft v1 for dogfooding). Source: Greg via Advisor #1009: "for every handoff/wait, who owns it, what starts next, the named dependency/result, where it is recorded, who/what sends the wake, and the recovery route if delivery fails". This is a working procedure, not automation; it carries no authority beyond Greg's word.

THE RULE. A session may end a turn while it still has work only if it has written a WAIT LINE and the wait has a WAKE SENDER that actually exists. "Waiting for a turn boundary", "waiting for a credit line" or "the host will notice" have no wake sender. For those, don't end the turn: check the condition now, or message the coordinator "wake me at T because X", and end only after that message is sent.

WAIT LINE: one status note on the held item (`engram work note REF --status "WAIT ..."`), or, with no held item, one mailbox message to the coordinator. Six fields:
  OWNER: the waiting session.
  ON: the named dependency with its exact id (delegation id, test-run id, mailbox and expected sender, item ref).
  WAKE: who or what sends the wake, and through which route.
  NEXT: the exact first action on waking.
  BY: the time the result is expected (UTC).
  RECOVERY: who checks at BY plus a margin, and what they do.
Example: "WAIT OWNER Opus ON evaluator delegation-X for w-14ce WAKE TermAl fan-in wait W NEXT done-check then commit BY 19:20Z RECOVERY Fable checks at 19:35Z: status, then mailbox wake".

STANDARD WAITS (WAKE / RECOVERY):
1. Full or focused gate, a detached launcher with --notify to the coordinator. WAKE: launcher, then coordinator mailbox; the coordinator checks expectedFingerprint = before = after, then relays to the owner. RECOVERY: the coordinator reads results.json at BY+15 min; the owner names the run id in its wait line.
2. Review pair or evaluator. WAKE: TermAl fan-in to the owner (termal_resume_after_delegations wait id in the wait line). RECOVERY: the coordinator sees the owner idle past BY+15 min and sends a mailbox wake; the owner then reads the results with termal_get_session_result.
3. Coordinator decision, concurrence or landing window. WAKE: the coordinator's mailbox message. RECOVERY: the coordinator owns BY; if it needs another party, it says so and gives a new BY.
4. Peer reply (another coordinator, an architect, the Advisor). WAKE: the peer's mailbox reply. RECOVERY: the waiter re-pings at BY on its next wake; after a second miss it reports a stop to the coordinator or Advisor.
5. Master moves (an item waiting for another landing). WAKE: the coordinator, after verifying the landing, sends "master is X" to every waiting coder. RECOVERY: the coder's wait line names the item it waits on.
6. Focus or naming binding (takes effect next turn). Avoid it: do the binding first, then other work, in the same turn. If a turn must end for it, message the coordinator "wake me, binding only"; the coordinator wakes immediately on receipt.
7. Pre-push notice: NOT a wait. The coder messages the coordinator and pushes in the same turn.

COORDINATOR DUTIES. On every wake: read all mailboxes; list sessions; for each window holder idle past the BY in its wait line, or with no wait line, send a mailbox wake. The coordinator's own waits follow the same rule. Its recovery is the Advisor: when the coordinator waits on Greg or the Advisor, it says so with a BY.

KNOWN GAP (stated, not hidden). Without a timer, a deadline check happens only when the checker is woken by something. If every session is idle waiting on another with no registered mechanism, nothing fires. Greg's direction is to make the procedure explicit before automating it (w-4e75a5319cde and w-3123ce57e780 are parked).
